mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between GDPC1 YoY < -2% and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6% for two months in a walk-forward validation.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation between INDPRO < -0.5% monthly changes and S&P 500 20-day returns in out-of-sample periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 1% for two consecutive months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising AND CPIAUCSL < 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL < 1% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous year's maximum for four consecutive months signals a housing market boom, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > max(HOUST last 12 months) for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained above-peak housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates labor market churning, which can foreshadow earnings volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases over 2 months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation between simultaneous increases in PAYEMS and UNRATE over two months and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below -5% signals a consumption-driven recovery, which boosts corporate sales expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS annualized change < -5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS annualized decline < -5% for three months.
